scope: Independent review of the corrected A01C/002 candidate and its 288 original-byte cases. MMIO is synthetic; no hardware behavior is inferred.
checks: Decoded the 142-byte body A01C..A0AA from pinned firmware bytes; the trailing NOP at A0AA and literal pool remain outside the body.
The body enforces exact mode 2/3, R1==0 and R3<=31. Mode 2 bounds R2 below 65536 and forms target 0x40010400; mode 3 bounds R2 below 16777216 and forms 0x40010500.

Mode 2 masks with 0xFF0000FF then inserts R2 in bits 23..8; mode 3 retains the low byte and inserts R2 in bits 31..8. Both paths perform a fresh second read before replacing bits 7..3 with R3, then return zero. Rejection branches return the pinned error literal.

Reran all 288 cases in an isolated directory; rows match exactly. Valid rows show exactly two reads and two ordered word writes at the selected address. Rejected rows have no MMIO access. R4/R5/R6 and SP are restored as recorded.
limitations: The second read observes the preceding write in these emulator fixtures. Real peripheral changes between accesses, bus semantics and concurrent updates are not modeled.
No caller reachability or canonical admission is implied.
